segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Three. Cut off from the greater of two unequal segments a segment equal to the less. Given two unequal segments A B and C, where A B is greater, we are to cut off from A B a segment equal to C.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Three. Cut off from the greater of two unequal segments a segment equal to the less. Given two unequal segments A B and C, where A B is greater, we are to cut off from A B a segment equal to C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: At point A, construct segment A D equal to segment C. Next, construct circle A D, with center A and defining radius point D, intersecting segment A B at point E.

subsegments.text: At point A, construct segment A D equal to segment C. Next, construct circle A D, with center A and defining radius point D, intersecting segment A B at point E.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since A is the center of circle A D, segment A E equals segment A D. And segment C also equals segment A D by construction. Because both A E and C equal A D, things equal to the same thing are equal to one another. Therefore segment A E has been cut off from the greater segment A B equal to the lesser segment C, as was required to do.
